items.title: The checklist is derived from the spec at the cut, one item per stamped scenario
Zero verdicts records nothing
An item nobody graded is scored as a fail
A step with no definition makes the result broken
The tests check requires results
A commit that is not a cut is refused
The clean room is the cut's committed files minus the denied ones, as one root commit
A scenario with two ids fails the spec check
An id used by two scenarios fails the spec check
Each level is accepted
A scenario with no level fails the spec check
A scenario with two levels fails the spec check
A need tag on the feature is inherited by every scenario under it
A scenario that traces to no need fails the spec check
A need tag naming no declared need fails the spec check
The spec check accepts a scenario tagged @wip
A feature file using every supported construct passes the check
An unknown keyword is refused with its line
A feature file holds exactly one feature
The stamper gives every unstamped scenario the next id from the ledger
Stamping twice changes nothing
A deleted scenario's id is never issued again
The id does not depend on the wording or the location
The id prefix is configuration
The release check refuses while any scenario is tagged @wip
The status report lists a scenario tagged @wip as planned
Status is derived from the results, never written
A scenario outline is one requirement, verified by all its rows
A passed result with the scenario's id verifies it
Any status but passed does not verify
One failing result among several fails the scenario
A scenario with no result is unverified, never left out
Tracing a need lists every scenario that traces to it, however it is tagged
A need nothing traces to says so
Tracing a scenario names its needs, its component and its bounded context
With results, the trace gives each scenario's status and the results behind it
An id that names nothing is refused
A results directory that does not exist is refused
Without results, the trace says no status was derived
A user need citing no source fails the spec check
A cycle records who built, graded and reads it, each as human or agent
A cycle whose builder is also its grader or spec owner is refused
A cycle that leaves a role unnamed is refused
A tag that is not an id, a level, a need or @wip fails the spec check
A scenario's result is labelled with its id, component and context
A scenario outline writes one result per example row, all with the outline's id
A failing step fails the result and names the step
A planned scenario is not run, and its result says it is planned
The runner runs every feature file the spec holds, found by looking, never listed
A run that finds no feature file is refused
A step is defined by a pattern and a function
Each step's return is the next step's context, and each scenario starts empty
A step two definitions match makes the result broken, naming both
A cycle is declared by hand in dhf/cycles/NN/cycle.edn
The score is written beside the cycle
Each task is run as rdm-spec <task>
A task that passes exits 0
A task that finds a problem exits 1 and names it on the error stream
A task that cannot run exits 2 and says why
An unknown task exits 2 and lists the tasks
The project scope keeps no implementation
A context scope removes that context's code and keeps the rest
A component scope removes that component's code and keeps the rest
A scope the model does not name is refused
A scenario with no id fails the spec check
The release check refuses a failed scenario
The release check refuses an unverified scenario
The release check passes when every scenario is verified
A scenario tagged @wip is planned whatever its results say
A task's results directory defaults to the configured one
A failing test command fails verification
A scope is the project, one context or one component, or a list of contexts and components
A verdict for an item not on the checklist is refused
Verify reads the cycle before anything else it does
A cycle with no cycle.edn is refused
The checkout's implementation is replaced by the room's, never merged with it
Edits the builder made outside the implementation are not used
The builder's tests are told where to write their results
The tests check passes when the builder's tests pass and every scenario's results passed
A scenario no test names fails verification
A spec file naming a configured stack word fails the spec check
checklist.json has one shape
A cut holding an unstamped scenario has no checklist
A verdicts file is a vector of id, verdict and evidence
A malformed verdicts file is refused and nothing is written
A cycle whose verification did not pass is not scored
Verify writes ratified.edn with the cut, the room's tree, the outcome and every check
A failed verification is recorded with its reason
A cut holding an unstamped scenario is not verified
A failed or broken result fails verification
A task's results directory is --results, else RESULTS_DIR, else the configured one
A task that names a cut reads the spec as it was at that cut
The kernel is a scope like a bounded context
A list of scopes removes the code of each, and keeps the rest
An id the ledger never issued fails the spec check
A task with no gate reports the findings of every stage
Each clause of the cut's clause lists is an item after the scenarios
The release check refuses a clause no audit tag names
A cycle scoped away from the compliance context carries no clause item
The release check refuses a controlled document with no id
A need's trace is one map under :trace
An outline with a row that has no result is unverified
Uncommitted and ignored files never reach a clean room
A kept file carrying a removed implementation file's bytes stops the fence
A committed path neither denied nor kept fails the check
A path under dhf/ is classified on its own
Results that name no row do not verify an outline
The status result is exactly this shape
A scenario's result carries each Allure element, filled from the scenario
An outline row's values are the result's parameters, and its history is the row's
A result that did not pass says why, in Allure's statusDetails
Evidence a step attaches is an Allure attachment
Verify reports every declared check, in order, with its outcome and margin
The first check that fails stops the gate, and the rest are named as not run
A configuration verify cannot trust is refused before anything runs
A check whose command is not found refuses the gate
A served app that answers and passes its probe passes, with its margin
An app that does not answer within its budget fails, naming the budget
A port already held refuses the gate rather than measure another process
An app that answers but fails its probe is not this application
A command that answers otherwise than expected fails the check
Failed is a Then that did not hold; broken is anything else that went wrong
Results go to the configured results directory when RESULTS_DIR is not set
A component the cut removed is fenced by the files the code layout finds for it
A result that breaks the mapping fails the tests check, naming the scenario and the element
A mapping verify cannot read is refused before anything runs
A configuration with no :allure is held to rdm-spec's default mapping
An app that accepts connections but never sends an HTTP response does not answer
A port held only by the closing connections of an app that has gone is free
A planned scenario's result is held to its spec label only
The plugins are the configuration's :plugins, in this shape
A declaration rdm-spec cannot trust is refused before anything runs
A subscriber is given the event on its standard input
Plugins run in the order declared, after the core's own stages
A plugin subscribing to an event a task does not publish does not run in that task
What a plugin says becomes the task's own report
A plugin that runs past its time limit is stopped and named as having timed out
A plugin whose command cannot be started cannot run
Gate plugins run before fence and verify, in the order declared, and stop them while one fails
A Gate plugin is given the task it gates
plugin add copies a template into the project and says how to declare it
plugin add never overwrites and never guesses
A :plugin check passes, fails or cannot run as its plugin answers
A Check plugin is asked in the checkout, with its cycle and cut
A :plugin check naming no plugin answering :Check is refused before anything runs
rdm-spec carries the same templates however it was installed
A probe is given the app's url, ending in "/", and has its own time limit
A probe that runs past its time limit is stopped and named as having timed out
A task that reads a cut reads the project's folder at the cut
A cut is read as committed, however the project's working tree differs
The room's implementation reaches the checkout as git would commit it
The verdicts of several files are filed as one
Verdicts across files are held to the same rules as one file
A plugin's :env is its environment, beside RDM_SPEC
A subscriber to :CycleVerified runs after verify passes, given the cycle
A cycle that is not verified publishes nothing
Several specs are the configuration's :specs, each a folder of its own
A configuration of several specs rdm-spec cannot read apart is refused before anything runs
Each spec is checked on its own terms, and one spec's finding fails the check
Each spec stamps from its own ledger, with its own prefix
A cycle may be scoped to one spec
Status and release read every spec, or the one named
A Check plugin's results are held to the mapping, and count
